points.why: It shows that homelessness, unlike potholes, reacts to interventions and has many causes, but it never says the definition is disputed or that there is no natural stopping point.
It treats housing costs, health services, the magnet effect and enforcement as interacting parts of one system that are all partly right, not as competing single causes.
It raises the regional boundary and suggests piloting and reallocating, but never recommends drawing out views from homeless people, providers or neighboring cities.
It keeps the headline count but adds flow, return and sheltered/unsheltered measures alongside it.

pitfalls.why: It rejects the single-cause pothole framing and declines to fund just one cause.

notes: Saying to 'settle the causal debate with local data' implies the problem has one resolvable answer that HMIS data can deliver, which understates how contested it is.
